subject: c12-chem
scope: CBSE Class XII Chemistry (043) 2026–27 written/theory Board-exam preparation; practical/internal-assessment material excluded.

chapters.name: Solutions
tips: Keep molarity and molality distinct; check whether temperature can affect the concentration expression.
For colligative properties, identify the correct property and apply the van't Hoff factor when abnormal association or dissociation is involved.
In numerical questions, write the known quantities and units before substituting.
Check whether the question asks for molar mass, elevation/depression or osmotic pressure before choosing the relation.
Link abnormal molar mass to association/dissociation rather than treating it as an unrelated exception.
common_mistakes: Applying colligative-property relations without checking the van't Hoff factor.

chapters.name: Electrochemistry
tips: Identify anode and cathode from oxidation and reduction rather than relying only on sign memory.
Write the overall cell reaction before constructing the Nernst reaction quotient.
Keep conductance, conductivity and molar conductivity distinct.
For electrolysis, track charge passed and electron stoichiometry carefully.
Connect batteries, fuel cells and corrosion to electrochemical-cell principles.
common_mistakes: Using the Nernst equation with an incorrect reaction quotient.

chapters.name: Chemical Kinetics
tips: Identify the reaction order before choosing an integrated rate equation or half-life relation.
Keep rate units separate from rate-constant units.
For Arrhenius questions, identify the quantities being compared before substituting.
Use concentration data exactly as specified; do not mix initial and instantaneous values.
Connect collision theory with activation energy and temperature dependence.
common_mistakes: Mixing zero-order and first-order equations/half-life relations.
Confusing rate-constant units with reaction-rate units.

chapters.name: d- and f-Block Elements
tips: Revise periodic position and electronic configuration before transition-metal trends.
Separate general transition-metal behaviour from specific exceptions and compounds.
Learn important compounds with their preparation, properties and uses.
Keep lanthanoids and actinoids distinct.
Use a compact trend table for repeated revision.
common_mistakes: Memorising trends without distinguishing exceptions and compounds.

chapters.name: Coordination Compounds
tips: Identify central metal, ligands, coordination number and oxidation state before naming a complex.
Apply nomenclature systematically.
Classify the relevant types of isomerism from the actual structure.
Use Werner's theory and bonding concepts to explain geometry and coordination number.
Check the overall complex charge before calculating oxidation state.
common_mistakes: Losing track of ligand names, coordination number, oxidation state, geometry or isomerism.

chapters.name: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes
tips: Identify the substrate class and C–X bond before choosing a reaction.
Keep substitution and elimination reactions distinct.
Remember that haloarenes do not behave exactly like haloalkanes.
Write reagents and conditions along with reactions.
Revise polyhalogen compounds with their prescribed uses.
common_mistakes: Writing organic reactions without checking reagent, condition, substrate class and major product.

chapters.name: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
tips: Classify the alcohol, phenol or ether before predicting its reaction.
Distinguish reactions of alcohols from reactions of phenols.
Track oxidation products carefully for primary and secondary alcohols.
Learn commercially important alcohols with their uses.
For ethers, identify the groups and conditions before predicting cleavage products.
common_mistakes: Writing organic reactions without checking reagent, condition, substrate class and major product.

chapters.name: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
tips: Identify aldehyde, ketone or carboxylic acid before selecting a reaction.
Organise carbonyl reactions by reagent and product.
Check oxidation/reduction conditions carefully.
Use structural formulas when distinguishing similar carbonyl compounds.
Connect carboxylic-acid acidity, preparation, reactions and uses.
common_mistakes: Writing organic reactions without checking reagent, condition, substrate class and major product.

chapters.name: Amines
tips: Classify the amine before discussing basicity or chemical behaviour.
Keep basicity trends separate from nucleophilic reactions.
Learn diazotisation and coupling as a connected sequence.
Track the aromatic ring and diazonium group carefully.
Use reaction maps for synthesis involving diazonium salts.
common_mistakes: Confusing amine basicity trends or mixing diazotisation and coupling conditions.

chapters.name: Biomolecules
tips: Organise carbohydrates by type, monomer and examples.
Connect proteins with amino acids, peptide linkage and function.
Learn enzymes through their catalytic role.
Use a compact table for vitamins and prescribed functions.
Distinguish nucleic acids and hormones by structure and function.
common_mistakes: Memorising classifications without connecting monomers, linkages, functions and examples.

order: Do Solutions, Electrochemistry and Chemical Kinetics first; practise their numerical patterns immediately after learning each concept.
Study d- and f-Block with a compact trend/compound sheet and revise it repeatedly rather than cramming once.
Complete Coordination Compounds next, especially terminology, nomenclature, isomerism and bonding.
Study the organic sequence in order: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes → Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers → Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids → Amines.
Finish Biomolecules with linked tables for carbohydrates, proteins, enzymes, vitamins, nucleic acids and hormones.
After the first complete pass, practise mixed conversion/reaction questions and numerical questions together.
Use the official sample paper and marking scheme to check answer style and coverage.
